findings.message: the pattern matches 6 of 10 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'Invalid user nuno from 172.21.0.3 port 36658'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:src_ip}, which fails on 'nuno from 172.21.0.3 port 36658'. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} It also misses lines of other shapes: 'Invalid user operator from 172.21.0.3 port 58444'; 'Invalid user git from 172.21.0.3 port 58468'; 'Connection closed by 172.21.0.3 port 58450'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
'reason' appears in 10/10 samples but is neither mapped nor listed as unresolved.

If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

the IR maps 'method', 'outcome', but no pattern captures them: the patterns capture only 'src_ip', 'src_port', 'user'. A mapping whose key is never extracted leaves its ECS field empty on every line. Add a named capture for each of these keys where its value sits in the line, or move the key to `unresolved`.
